title: 2026 budget process and 5 percent levy target
subtitle: Committee also backed a call for federal and provincial tariff stimulus funding and moved away from a budget subcommittee.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee set the direction for the 2026 Plan and Budget. It recommended the review timetable in report COR-CFN-25-009. It also asked that any budget increase involving new staff positions come with a budget issue paper. The report was referred to the May 21 Council meeting, where staff will revise the timetable first. Committee members agreed not to repeat last year's budget subcommittee.

The committee recommended that staff prepare a draft 2026 budget for direct regional services with a tax levy increase of no more than 5 percent {{vote:m3}}. Staff called this challenging but achievable. Council can still approve a higher or lower levy at final budget, so the figure is a starting point for staff rather than a hard cap. For residents, it signals that affordability will shape the budget, and that some service changes may be listed for Council to consider.

The committee also recommended that Council call on the federal and provincial governments to fast-track municipal stimulus funding in response to US tariffs {{vote:m5}}. The funding would cover infrastructure, transit and housing, including social housing supports. Council will consider these recommendations later.

decisions.item: 2026 Plan and Budget process and principles
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the 2026 budget review timetable, forwarding the report to the Police Services Board and area municipalities, and requiring a budget issue paper for any increase that adds staff positions, with the item referred to the May 21 Council meeting.

The committee recommended directing staff to present a draft 2026 budget for direct regional services with a tax levy increase of no more than 5 percent {{vote:m3}}, while Council keeps the ability to approve a different amount.

decisions.item: Ending debate on the budget cap
decisions.detail: The committee agreed to call the previous question on the budget cap motion, ending debate so the main motion could be voted on {{vote:m4}}.

The committee recommended that Council ask the federal and provincial governments for municipal stimulus strategies funding infrastructure, housing, transit and social housing supports, and send the resolution to area municipalities, associations and government officials {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Councillors broadly opposed a budget subcommittee, saying it left members who were not on it without the full discussion, and preferred that all of Council hear delegations and information together.

Several councillors supported keeping the deadline for budget motions so staff can review financial impacts. Staff said last-minute motions on budget day previously forced long recesses. Others suggested adding an extra budget day so tough choices are not made late at night.

On the 5 percent target, some councillors wanted it to have real force, while others worried a hard cap was unrealistic given tariffs, layoffs and growing demand for services. Staff and the Clerk's office said Council could still approve a higher or lower levy.

One councillor questioned whether the cap meaningfully constrains anything if staff also present a list of optional add-ons. The mover said the aim was to have staff start from essential services first, with other items debated separately.

Other process points raised were separating capital from operating discussions, setting aside more time for questions during the police budget presentation, and scheduling conflicts with the proposed November budget dates.
